name: James Clark Ross in the Ross Sea
summary: Sent to find the south magnetic pole, the Erebus and the Terror force their way through the pack ice into an open sea that now bears Ross's name. They chart the mountains of Victoria Land, see a volcano in eruption, which Ross names for his ship, and sail for 400 kilometres along a wall of ice as high as the cliffs of Dover: the Great Ice Barrier. It was the farthest south anyone had been.

stops.note: The Erebus and the Terror sail in September.
Governor John Franklin builds them an observatory.
Through the pack into open water, and a coast of high mountains.
A volcano in eruption, smoking above the ice.
Cliffs of ice along which they sail east for days, finding no way through.
After a second season in the Ross Sea, round to the Atlantic.
The east side of the Antarctic Peninsula.
Home after four and a half years.

informs.note: Victoria Land and the Great Ice Barrier charted
